Objectives:
The primary goal of this burn is to use fire to top kill 60% of 
small Juniper trees ( <6') that are trying to invade the grassland mesa tops.

Reduce the old decadent growth grasses by 90% to enhance herbaceous and browse availability and palatability for, both livestock and wildlife
Planned_Implementation:
The proposed action is to burn approximately 150 acres of
pinyon-juniper grassland on the West Mesa and approximately
another 120 acres on the Airport Mesa areas using BLM personnel
and equipment. Scattered slash piles throughout Fort Stanton
and the Lincoln Valley will be burnt during the winter months
to remove unwanted debris and fuel loading. (See the attached
map for slash pile locations).
All fire activities would occur off of maintained roads and
existing two track roads. All terrain vehicles (ATV's) within
the burn area may be needed to monitor fire activities and
transport equipment etc. Some of the two-track roads have been
closed to recreational uses for the purpose of protecting
natural resource.


West Mesa RX is scheduled for burning to start April 15. Over the past two years fires that have occurred
in the Ruidoso Area have resulted in the cancellation this Prescribed fire. I would like to consider doing this
burn earlier then originally planned. Starting as soon as possible from to days date (03/05/2003). The
original Resource objective was to top kill 60% small Juniper trees {<6&$). Reduce old decadent growth
grasses by 90% to enhance herbaceous and browse for wildlife. Reduce hazardous fuel loads by 90% over
the project area.
Reduction of hazardous fuels was completed in 2002 by mechanical removal (lop and scatter) of trees in
the project area. This will reduce the fire intensity that was originally called for, to top kill 60% of small
juniper trees ( <6 &$). A low intensity fire can now be backed through the burn area that would target small
Juniper trees under 2&$ and remove ground litter produced the mechanical work applied in 2002.
The original burn plan also called for burning Monday-Friday, I would also like to open this up to seven
days to include Saturday and Sunday should conditions to complete the burn project be in prescription on
these days.

Trt_Concerns_Desc:
This burn plan is an updated version of the original Mesa Chivato Prescribed Fire Plan,
signed in August 29, 2005. The purpose of the update is to enter the plan into the new NWCG
interagency template format, renew signatures and address any specific issues which may have
changed such as: NEPA, Threatened and Endangered Species, unit/s to be burned, new charge
numbers or permit numbers, maps of the target/MMA area, specific safety concerns to the area,
organization, ignition sequence/operation etc ...
This plan covers prescribed fires within the Ignacio Chavez and Chamisa WSA's on
Mesa Chivato which is located approximately 50 air miles North West of Albuquerque. There
are 9 separate units with 17, 751 total acres within their perimeter. The purpose for these burns is:
l) to reduce fuel loading, ladder fuels, stand densities and open up crown canopies, which under
the right conditions could contribute to high intensity crown fire and 2) Maintain historically
open meadows and grasslands which are being encroached upon by pinon, juniper and ponderosa
pine trees. Historic uses and active fire suppression have interrupted the natural fire regime in
this fire dependent ecosystem. This has resulted in a reduction in the natural vegetative
production and has degraded the community structure normally found in a ponderosa parkland
ecosystem, and the pinon/juniper invasion will continue to expand and displace the understory
vegetation.

Objectives: 1.  Improve vegetative resources within the NCA.\r\n2.  Enhance wildlife habitat and watershed values.\r\n3.  Restore the "historic&& fire regime within the project area.
Planned_Implementation:
Pre-burn work: (location & description of black lines, holding lines, etc.)
Roads, drainage bottoms, hand line and wet line will be utilized as the primary boundaries to
check any fire spread outside of the designated burn units. The roads that will be utilized as
unit boundaries will be brushed and any ladder fuels next to the road will be removed. Hand
line and/or wet line between natural barriers will be utilized to protect the parcels of private
property in sections IO and 22. The wildlife improvements within the project area will require
hand line and/or wet line for protection. A 1000-gallon portable tank will be set up and filled
in an accessible area to provide a water source for the engines. Prior to any ignition a recon
will be conducted to assure that the area is clear of any civilians.
Any blackline operations will be completed in the low to the desired intensity prescription
range (see Weather, Fuel and Fire Parameters, pages 8 & 9)
BLOCK I: May be burnt in conjunctions with Block 3. Depending on conditions either
handline or wetline in conjunction with blackline will be utilized in the northeast comer of the
unit to protect private lands located in section 10. The two track roads located to the north,
west, south and east will be utilized as control lines. One track will be cleared of debris to
mineral soil prior to any ignition operations. Any ladder fuels next to the control lines will be
removed. The range improvement water system located on the northern and western perimeters
consists of plastic pipe and valves. There are also steel tanks, plastic pipe, and valves on the
south side of Cerro Piedrita. The water system will be protected by scratch line, and wet line.
There is a Cultural Site located on top of the continental divide in the southeast comer of the
unit that consists of wood debris along with artifacts dating to before World War II. The
Cultural Site will be protected by handline, wetline and blackline. The Cultural Site (Sawmill)
located between Blocks 1 and 2 on the eastern perimeter of Block 1 will also be protected by
handline, wetline, and blackline. Hand line will be constructed well away from the site to
provide a buffer and a Type IV or VI engine will be made available to protect the site during
ignition operations adjacent to the site.
BLOCK 2: The two track roads located to the north, west, south, and the east will be utilized
as control lines. One track will be cleared of debris to mineral soil prior to any ignition
operations. Any ladder fuels next to the control lines will be removed. The Cultural Site
located on the northern perimeter between Blocks 1 and 2 (Sawmill) will be protected by
handline, wetline, and blackline. Hand line will be constructed well away from the site to
provide a buffer and a Type IV or VI engine will be made available to protect the site during
ignition operations adjacent to the site. The private land and the Cultural Site that consists of 3
structures will be protected by handline, wetline, and blackline. Handline will be constructed
from the end of the two track road in the southeast comer of the burn block, north along the
fence line to the northwest comer of sections 15 and 22, and continued east to county road 42.
BLOCK 3: May be burnt in conjunction with Block 1. Pre burn work discussed in Block 1
also applies to this Block. (see Block 1)
BLOCK 4 & 5: Two track roads make up the entire perimeter of Blocks 4 and 5. One track
will be cleared of debris to mineral soil prior to any ignition operations. Any ladder fuels next
to the control lines will be removed. The Cultural Site located to the west of Cerro Chato will
be protected by handline, wetline, and blackline. Access to the Cultural Site is limited.
Ignition plan:
Ignition plan common to all Burn Blocks: Hand ignition will be utilized to implement
ignition operations. Ignition will be conducted in a manner which allows for the most control
of active fire and smoke output, while providing for perimeter protection and burn crew safety.
Ignition will begin on the leeward side of the burn units and continue to the windward side of
the unit. Hand ignition will be utilized for any black lining operations along the roads and
along the private property boundaries. When sufficient black lines are achieved, hand ignition
will be utilized to ignite strip head fires in the interior portions of the burn units. Stripping
distance will vary depending on fire intensity.
Potential holding problems:
All efforts will be made to establish black line along the road and the hand line used to protect
the private property in the northeast corner of unit #1 and unit #2 (section 10), and the hand
line used to protect the private property on the eastern perimeter of unit #2 (section 22) and
along the reservation boundary in unit #5 (sections 18&19). Efforts will also be made to
protect the wildlife and water improvements located throughout the burn units.
Location of holding forces and instructions:
Holding forces will be working in conjunction with firing operations. One engine will be
utilized for holding/firing operations. When burning adjacent to any cultural site that has
access one engine will be utilized to hold and improve the site. The remainder of the forces
will be positioned at the discretion of the Holding Specialist. If a spot does occur all personnel
will work in conjunction with the engines. While burning areas with little or no threat of
escape, some holding forces may be utilized as part of the ignition crew. Patrols will be made
along the perimeter of the burn area to ensure no spotting is occurring down wind from the
firing operations.
Water sources:
T7N, Rl3W, Section 10 (Private Land, for emergency use only). The closest water source is
located at the El Malpais National Monument Work Center located on State Highway 53.
Approximately a 2 hour turn around time.
Under high end prescription parameters a 1000 gallon portable tank will be set up adjacent to
the target Burn Block prior to ignition.
Allowable areas:
10,500 Acres
Public safety provisions:
-Public information will be provided prior to and during any ignitions.
-News release prior to any ignition operations.
-Prescribed Fire In Progress signs will be posted on County rd. 42 and the Continental Divide
Trail heads.
-Personnel will be on site to control access into the project areas.
Counter measures for slop-overs:
Unless deemed more of a threat, all burning will stop and all efforts will be made to contain the
slop-over. The ignition team can be utilized as holding personnel. Opportunities exist to
utilize natural barriers, and two track roads as indirect control lines for any spot fires or slop
overs.
Any spot fires or slop overs occurring in adjacent burn blocks will be evaluated based upon
predicted weather, fire behavior, and expected impacts.

The Chain of Craters Prescribed fire is within the El Malpais National
Conservation Area and the Chain of Craters Wilderness Study Area. This project is located
approximately 30 miles southwest of Grants on the Cerro Brillante Quadrangle in T7N, R 13W, Sections?,
8, 9, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, and 22. The project area consists of 4,861 acres (see burn area
description) of ponderosa pine, pinyon, juniper, grass, and brush. This is a hazardous fuels reduction and
SYKES Act project. The goal of this project is to employ management ignited prescribed fire in the
pin yon, juniper, and ponderosa pine to reduce stand densities, ladder fuels, and hazardous fuel loadings
that contribute to the decline of wildlife habitat and the potential of catastrophic wildfire.
